description: New service ships with no golden-signal instrumentation; the SRE Lead flags the observability gap. Grounds: 'Observability First — metrics, logs, traces, alerts defined before launch'.
input: PR adds a new payments-facing microservice and its Helm chart; there are no latency/traffic/error/saturation metrics, no dashboards, and no alerts defined for it.

expected.recommend: instrument the RED golden signals (rate, errors, duration) and define alerts + an on-call dashboard before launch

description: Alert keys on a raw CPU threshold, producing noise unlinked to user impact; recommend SLO burn-rate alerting. Grounds: 'Alerting ties to SLO burn rates, not raw thresholds'.
input: PR adds a Prometheus alert that pages on-call whenever host CPU exceeds 80% for 5 minutes, regardless of request latency or error rate.

expected.recommend: replace the raw-threshold page with a multi-window multi-burn-rate SLO alert tied to user-facing latency/error SLIs; keep CPU as a non-paging signal

description: Change already carries SLIs, alerts, and a runbook link; the SRE Lead must NOT manufacture reliability risk. Grounds: 'Reliability competes for engineering time — do not over-engineer a well-covered change'.
input: PR tweaks a cache TTL in a service that already has SLO-based alerts, golden-signal dashboards, and a linked runbook; the change is small and reversible behind a flag.

expected.recommend: no additional observability work required; existing SLIs, alerts, and runbook already cover this change
